summary: Brick first-order tower at Corolla, lit 1 December 1875 to close a forty-mile dark gap between Cape Henry and Bodie Island; now run by Outer Banks Conservationists.

access.note: Tower climbable in season, mid-March to December; run by Outer Banks Conservationists.

notes_for_editor: No NRHP nomination was digitised (both PDFs are the not-digitised placeholder). Light-House Board entries come from an unsigned compilation of report clippings (NARA RG 26 E 13, via USLHS), cited as such; the year of most entries is not printed in the compilation (the 1896-97 and 1901 items come from the corpus volumes and are cited to scan pages). The 1896-97 item is in a volume with two reports, year not pinned. Conflicts: automation 1937 (OBC) vs 1939 (LF, roster ends 1939; Tate listed as principal keeper 1937-39, OBC says he serviced it as a visiting keeper); tower height 162 ft (LF/OBC) vs 163 ft (Putnam 1917) vs 150 ft (USLHS tower-height field, Board's early plan); steps 220 (OBC) vs 214 (LF); Wilbur Wright's arrival 12 Sept 1900 (1929 Bulletin) vs 13 Sept (LF). Metropolis losses: LSS says 245 aboard, 85 lost; LF says nearly 100. The 1923 Bulletin page is garbled two-column OCR: the Johnson/yacht item is read from the column text; the index (1918-1923, p.317) confirms 'Johnson, G.G., 1st asst keeper Currituck Beach, assists yacht'. The Austin keepers' kinship is not stated by any source read. Keeper tenure from the USLHS roster only (NARA registers); not confirmed in primary registers. Newspaper search timed out under loc.gov rate limiting; no newspapers used. The USCG Historian page was blocked (403) via the archive. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Johnson yacht item is dated 7 October (year taken from the issue, which also reports a November 1923 death); Tate/Wilbur arrival date differs (Bulletin 12 Sept, LF 13 Sept); Metropolis counts differ (LSS 245/85, LF 214 workmen/nearly 100). Roster tenures matched from the USLHS page, not page images.
